newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev eases on c.bank dollar buying-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev eases on c.bank dollar buying-dealers.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev eased to 1,498-1,502 per dollar in mid-afternoon from the opening's 1,493-1,499 due to dollar buying by the central bank, dealers said.
"The lev dipped after the central bank started bidding for foreign currency at 1,497-1,499 (levs per dollar) in the afternoon," a commercial bank dealer said.
Central bank officials were not available for comment.
The lev has idled near opening levels in thin trade until the central bank came to the market because dollar demand from customers and commercial banks was low, traders said.

The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) has been seen as a major foreign currency buyer on the local interbank market since March, capping the upside for the lev and boosting its reserves to $1.146 billion at end-April from $554 million in March.
The lev gained to its current levels from around 1,800 at the beginning of March due to increased foreign curency supply from both local and foreign investors opting for high yield local debt paper.

Pending sell-offs have also attracted investors in local treasury paper because some Bulgarian government securities, the so-called bad debt bonds or ZUNKs can be used as means of payment in privatisation deals at par value while now they trade around 50 percent of par. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
